subtitle.simple: Why one new rule sent millions of Windows PCs to the blue screen.
subtitle.tech: Channel File 291: 21 fields in the template, 20 inputs from the sensor, out-of-bounds read.

headline.simple: Problem: On July 19, 2024, millions of Windows PCs show a blue screen. Why?
headline.tech: Bug: Out-of-bounds read in the Content Interpreter – 21 fields expected, 20 supplied.

text.simple: On your PC a program opens a connection, and the guard notices.
text.tech: A process opens a named pipe; the Falcon sensor captures the IPC event.

text.simple: The guard gives the rule checker 20 details about the program.
text.tech: The sensor passes the Content Interpreter an input array with 20 entries.

text.simple: The rule checker looks it up: the rules have 21 fields, but field 21 has never mattered.
text.tech: The IPC template type defines 21 fields; existing instances use a wildcard for field 21.

text.simple: It compares details 1 to 20, skips the unused field 21, and reports: harmless.
text.tech: Inputs 0 to 19 are matched; the wildcard never reads input 20.

text.simple: On July 19, CrowdStrike ships new rules that check field 21 for real for the first time.
text.tech: 2024-07-19: New template instances with a real criterion on field 21 instead of a wildcard.

text.simple: The inspection lets the new rules through because it doesn't notice the guard gives only 20 details.
text.tech: A logic error in the Content Validator lets the instances pass despite 21 fields.

text.simple: The inspection sends the new rule file to millions of PCs worldwide, including yours.
text.tech: 04:09 UTC: The Channel File 291 update goes out to all Windows sensors.

text.simple: Again a program opens a connection, and the guard gives only 20 details, as always.
text.tech: Next IPC event; the sensor again passes only 20 inputs.

text.simple: The rule checker loads the new rules and compares details 1 to 20.
text.tech: The interpreter loads the new instance and matches inputs 0 to 19.

text.simple: For field 21 it reaches for detail 21, which doesn't exist, and grabs at nothing.
text.tech: Access to input 20 of a 20-entry array: out-of-bounds read with no bounds check.

text.simple: Because the guard sits deep inside Windows, its crash takes all of Windows down: blue screen.
text.tech: The exception occurs in the kernel driver and cannot be caught: BSOD.

text.simple: On restart the guard loads the same rule file right away, and Windows crashes again.
text.tech: The sensor reloads Channel File 291 at boot: boot loop until manual repair.

headline.simple: Solution: The inspection counts the details, and the rule checker never reaches into nothing again.
headline.tech: Fix: The validator checks the input count; the interpreter gets a runtime bounds check.

text.simple: The inspection now counts: the rule needs 21 details, but the guard gives only 20.
text.tech: The validator compares the instance's field count with the inputs the sensor supplies.

text.simple: The inspection stops the rule and sends it back; not a single PC gets it.
text.tech: The instance is rejected and not shipped as a channel file.

text.simple: Stress test: Suppose a rule file like this still reaches your PC one day.
text.tech: Stress test: A faulty instance reaches the sensor anyway.

text.simple: A program acts, the guard gives 20 details, and the rule checker loads the new rules.
text.tech: IPC event, 20 inputs; the interpreter loads the faulty instance.

text.simple: New: Before field 21, the rule checker checks that detail 21 exists, and safely skips the rule.
text.tech: New runtime bounds check: index 20 is out of range, so the instance is discarded without a read.

text.simple: The rule checker reports: harmless, and the guard keeps working normally.
text.tech: Result with no match returned to the sensor; no crash.

text.simple: Result: Windows keeps running, no blue screen.
text.tech: Result: no BSOD, even if a faulty instance slips through.
